text: Every meeting ends the same way. Someone takes attendance, chases down who was missing, and turns scattered notes into minutes. That's eight to ten minutes, after every single session.
The AI notetakers captured the conversation, but none of them tracked attendance, or participant telemetry. And there was no central view of who actually showed up, or for how long.

So ByteIT built an end-to-end meeting intelligence loop. Five tools, working as one: Google Calendar, the Google Meet v2 API, Google Drive and Docs, Fathom AI, and a self-hosted n8n automation engine.
Here's how it works. First, a scheduled scan pulls events from Google Calendar, and filters out anything that isn't a real meeting. Out-of-office blocks, prayer times, and breaks.
Next, the Google Meet API retrieves the actual conference records, and matches each one to its calendar event, by meeting code, or by start-time proximity.
Then the engine calculates participant telemetry. Exact join and leave times, and total presence, down to the second. AI bots like Fathom are isolated, so they never distort human attendance.
It locates the meeting's Google Drive folder, and a multi-format date engine pairs today's session with its Gemini Notes document, no matter how the date is written.

Fathom's summary is cleaned up by an AI model, into key points, decisions, and action items. Finally, a filter guard skips ad-hoc or unrecorded calls, and a batch update writes everything into the Google Doc.
Under the hood, it's one n8n workflow, with custom JavaScript handling time zone normalization, time-window alignment, and conditional routing.

The result? One document per meeting. An attendance summary. A structured table of who was present or absent, with join time, leave time, and duration. A full participant log. And polished AI meeting notes.

Today, one hundred percent of targeted meetings are captured automatically. Producing minutes went from eight to ten minutes per meeting, to zero manual effort. And attendance precision now exceeds ninety-five percent.
Those saved hours now go into core projects, AI agent engineering, and strategic initiatives.
